Bundled verification tool: validates key chain integrity, bootloader lock state and environment anomalies. Use it to confirm that the built-in TEE key simulation and boot-state spoofing are actually working.

Known behaviour: this tool carries its own anti-interception probe — it imports a self-signed certificate under its own alias and reads it back. Once the engine covers it, the row “TrickyStore or a similar module detected” therefore ALWAYS appears; it does not mean the spoofing failed. Judge by the “bootloader locked / Google attestation root” rows, and by the TEE panel above for the engine verdict. Third-party checkers (vvb2060 Key Attestation, Play Integrity) have no such probe.

Recommended for kernels below 5.10: patches your stock boot image with the official Magisk patcher (unmodified magiskboot + boot_patch.sh bundled in this APK). On A-only legacy SAR devices pick the recovery image instead. Flash the result via fastboot/recovery; no root needed.
This APK does not bundle the Magisk payload (magiskboot / boot_patch.sh), so the Magisk route is unavailable.
Pass KEEPVERITY=true to Magisk (keep verity instead of stripping it). Off by default, same as Magisk default.
Pass KEEPFORCEENCRYPT=true to Magisk. Off by default, same as Magisk default.
Pass PATCHVBMETAFLAG=true to Magisk. Only for devices that need the vbmeta flags patched.
Pass RECOVERYMODE=true: patch a recovery image instead of boot. Needed on A-only system-as-root devices whose boot image has no ramdisk.
Pass LEGACYSAR=true: hexpatch skip_initramfs to want_initramfs in the kernel. Auto is Magisk\'s own test (the root of /proc/mounts is /dev/root); force it on if the kernel is not detected correctly.

The built-in TEE engine and the built-in TA companion ship with this app. They live in RAM only, so the module list cannot show them — that is why the switches are here. They default to ON (a missing switch file means on) and are independent; with them off nothing of the built-in modules is left on the device, and modules you flashed yourself are unaffected.

Note: the property spoofing is on while no TEE engine covers attestation — the two contradict each other (properties say locked, attestation says deviceLocked=false), which games and banking apps flag as an environment anomaly more readily. Either install the TEE engine or switch this off.
